question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & -3 & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & -3 & -1 & 8 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & -3 & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & -3 & -1 & 8 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-1R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & -3 & -1 & 8 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4 \\ 2 & 5 & -2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-1R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-1R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y-4z &=6 \\ -2x-2y+7z &=3 \\ -3y+6z &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & -2 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-2y-4z &=-2 \\ x-y-4z &=1 \\ -2x+6z &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -2 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -4 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-1 \\ y &=0-(-1)(-1) \\ &=-1 \\ x &=-1-(-1)(-1) \\ &\quad -(-2)(-1) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-4,-1,-1\right)
$$

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & -2 & 14\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-1R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$
